phase.name: foundation
phase.description: Fix the activity problem: get FIDE-rated games on the calendar. Baselines. Top two leaks. Narrow the repertoire.

targets.description: Mistakes and blunders with no tactical shape (judgement, not calculation)
targets.response: No puzzle fixes judgement. Unassisted annotation of your own long games, then engine comparison; calculation sets with no board movement; slower play.

success.rule: weighted frequency over 4 weeks at least 20% below baseline, on at least 30 games; otherwise 'no change' or 'worse'; fewer games -> 'not enough data'

targets.description: Errors made with under 30 seconds on the clock
targets.response: A clock rule in the long game: never move in a critical position under 20 seconds of thought; measured by fast_critical_errors.

where: lichess.org (rated, 45+15 pool or a club game)

sessions.success_criterion: One completed rated long game, PGN in the database by the nightly run.
sessions.notes: Play with the clock rule if a time leak is targeted. No blitz before the long game.

sessions.title: Unassisted annotation of tonight's game
sessions.success_criterion: Written annotation (critical moments, your own evals) saved before any engine use.

sessions.title: Calculation set: only-move positions from your own games
sessions.success_criterion: 15 positions, full variation written before revealing, no board movement; judgment_calibration score recorded.

sessions.title: Engine review of Monday's game against your annotation
sessions.success_criterion: Every error tagged by you first, then compared with the pipeline's tags; disagreements logged.
sessions.notes: Disagreements are the interesting part. They calibrate your judgement and catch tagger mistakes.

sessions.title: Repertoire audit: what do you actually play?

instructions: List every opening reached 5+ times in the last 12 months (see /chess/games).
Mark which are prepared and which are improvised.
Write the result into chess-coach/config/repertoire.yaml (white.first_move, lines with priority core/developing).

sessions.notes: Narrowing beats broadening at this level. Two lines as White, one reply each to e4/d4/c4 as Black is enough.

sessions.title: Rook endgame baseline
sessions.success_criterion: Each position played out from both sides; result vs theoretical result recorded (tablebase where ≤7 pieces).

Get FIDE-rated: find and register for a classical event

instructions: List every FIDE-rated classical event within reach of Turnhout in the next 6 months: Belgian interclubs, Belgian and Dutch opens, weekend events in northern France and western Germany.
Enter dates, deadlines and formats into chess-coach/config/calendar.yaml.
Register for at least one and set registered: true.
Check the next FIDE World Amateur Championship: dates, U2000 eligibility (no published rating ≥2000 in the prior year), entry deadline.

sessions.success_criterion: calendar.yaml has at least one event with registered: true.
sessions.notes: Both FIDE ratings are flagged inactive. Nothing else this week matters as much as this hour.

briefing.headline: You have played zero FIDE-rated classical games in twelve months, so Sunday's registration block is the most important hour of week 8.

situation.text: Your FIDE standard rating of 1795 is flagged inactive, with 0 rated games in the last 12 months. Modelled probability of reaching 2200 under the current scenario is 0.2 per cent; reaching 2000 sits at 27.3 per cent.
You played 0 rapid or classical games in the last 28 days, against 3 in the 28 days before that. Form data for the serious time controls is effectively absent.
The pool behind these numbers is 7,123 games, but only 6 are classical and 674 rapid; 6,327 are bullet or blitz. Every leak rate below is dominated by fast play.
This is a deload week (every fourth week), 6 hours total: tactics, openings and endgames are cut to 60 per cent, while play and review stay at full length.

focus.text: Primary target is positional mistakes and blunders with no tactical shape: 86.95 per 100 across 6,456 instances, severity 31.4. The four-week goal is 69.56 per 100, measured over at least 30 games between 9 November and 7 December.
A representative case is the rapid game where you played Qg4 instead of Nc5, costing 72.6 win percentage points with no tactical motif in the position.
Two classical examples show the same judgement failure in quieter settings: Rc1 instead of cxd4 lost 44.4 win percentage points, and Bg4 instead of Kg2 in a rook-and-bishop ending lost 41.5.

Secondary target is errors made with under 30 seconds on the clock: 41.98 per 100 over 4,961 instances, the highest severity of the two at 36.0. Target is 33.58 per 100 over the same window and the same 30-game minimum.

progress.text: The cycle starting 5 October returned no_change on positional blunders: baseline 86.66, measured 86.88 over 492 games. The 28 September cycle was the same verdict, 87.70 measured over 631 games.
Time-trouble errors came back worse in both recent cycles: 48.64 against a 41.83 baseline over 492 games, and 51.87 against 41.79 over 631 games. Neither cycle moved towards the 33.5 target.
The one leak trending better is endgame errors, down 21.1 per cent from 17.98 to 14.19 per 100 on matched samples of 149 and 149. That is a small sample and is not a target this week.

week_ahead.text: Monday is a 90-minute long game at 45+15 or slower, 60+30 where possible. Slow play is the only way to generate the classical sample you currently lack.

Monday's second block is 30 minutes of unassisted annotation of that game, and Wednesday's 36-minute engine review checks your annotation against the engine. That pairing is aimed directly at judgement errors with no tactical shape.
Tuesday and Saturday are 36-minute calculation sets built from only-move positions in your own games, the deload-reduced length.
Thursday is a 36-minute repertoire audit of what you actually play; Friday is a 36-minute rook endgame baseline.
Sunday is a 60-minute admin block to find and register for a classical event. Your registration window is already 37 days past, and you are flagged eligible.

caveats: The leak rates come from a pool of 7,123 games that is 89 per cent bullet and blitz, with only 6 classical games. They may not describe how you play at 45+15.
With 0 rapid or classical games in the last 28 days, there is no current form reading on accuracy or win rate.
Both targets require at least 30 games in the 9 November to 7 December window. Below that, the cycle cannot be scored.
All four headline leaks except endgame errors are flagged flat; recent swings of 11 to 14 per cent in fork and mate-in-n allowances sit on samples under 100 and should not be read as movement.
